title: Lightweight sketch profiling + shadow-apply batcher autopilot
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem: We need continuous, low-overhead batching recommendations that reduce per-token cost without surprising latency regressions. Existing heavy profiling jobs are accurate but too slow and expensive for per-route or per-tenant decisioning. This ticket proposes a lightweight sketch-based profiling pipeline plus a conservative shadow-apply rollout controller that can safely materialize suggested batch/cache configs into production.
background: Current profiling relies on full request capture + offline synthesis (expensive and high-latency). Operators want near-real-time recommendations for routes with bursty traffic or high KV cache reuse. The solution should be cheap to compute (amortized <1% CPU per router), robust to skewed workloads, and have built-in safety (shadow apply and automated rollback).
design_summary: 1) Ingest: router hooks emit compact signatures (route_id, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, kv_hit_flag) for each request. 2) Sketching: per-route Count-Min sketch + reservoir samples (k=100) to estimate request size distribution and prefix similarity without storing full request text. 3) Metrics: compute estimated effective batch size, expected latency (via microbench lookup table), and token-level cost delta using a simple cost model. 4) Heuristics + Bandit: candidate configs (batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, kv_window) are scored by deterministic heuristic rules then refined by a Thompson-sampling bandit to prefer safe wins. 5) Safety: recommendations are validated by a shadow-apply run (per-customer shadow traffic), then a staged canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers and an operator approval step for >25% changes.
implementation_details:
- Sketch storage: Redis streams / compact hashes with TTL=48h; sketches are aggregated in a lightweight service (batcher-prober).
- Sampling: reservoir sampling keeps representative payload examples used by the quality check (fidelity sampling).
- Microbench: precomputed latency/cost lookup table indexed by model, hw class, seq_len_bucket, and batch_size. Updated weekly from runtime perf jobs.
- Controller: continuous reconciler runs every 60s, proposes config deltas limited by max_delta_per_minute.
- Shadow-apply: dual-routing for a tiny fraction of requests (1-3%) into the new config but without exposing responses to customers; metrics are compared to baseline over a 30m window.
- Rollback criteria: immediate rollback if p95 latency increased by >15% absolute OR request error rate increased by >0.5 percentage points OR throughput drops causing SLA violations. Additionally, model-quality checks (eval prompts on reservoir samples) must not regress by >2% on key metrics.
- Observability: per-recommendation dashboard in Console showing expected savings, simulated latency delta, and risk score. All actions are auditable in the private control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Sketch-based profiles must estimate median and p95 request length within ±12% compared to ground-truth sampling for 90% of routes
End-to-end recommendation pipeline (ingest->sketch->score->shadow-apply->canary) runs with <60s latency from first observed signature to visible recommendation
Shadow-apply run produces no customer-visible deviations for canaries below 5% traffic and triggers rollback per the defined criteria when a regression occurs
Console displays per-route expected savings and a clear action button that starts the staged rollout with audit logging
Automated rollback fires under test harness scenarios and cancels staged ramps within 5 minutes of threshold crossing

Microbench: extend latency lookup table to include new seq_len_buckets - PR #5250
Controller: reconcile loop + bandit tuner prototype - PR #5271
Shadow-apply plumbing (dual-routing + isolated metric collection) - PR #5289
Console: UX for recommendation card and staged rollout controls - PR #5302
E2E tests: fuzz traffic generator to validate rollback thresholds - test plan doc
risks: Sketch cardinality may underperform on extremely sparse routes (cold start) - mitigated by reservoir fallback
False positives in rollback if noisy telemetry not smoothed - mitigated by EWMA smoothing and requiring sustained regression windows
Cost model mismatch for new hardware classes - mitigated by flagging unknown hw and falling back to conservative defaults
